podcast.body: Kino, with their singer Soi, released the song "Change" (translates from Russian) around 1989 during the last years of the Soviet period. This song quickly became a political rallying cry amidst the significant social and political changes occurring in 1989, 1990, and 1991. The band, like others, was allegedly part of a CIA operation to import subversive rock into the USSR, with claims that Soi was given songs written by Hollywood songwriters. "Kino and their singer Soi from 1989. The song is called Change and yes it did become something of a political rally and cry in those fast changing days of 1989, 1990 and 1991."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Recorded by Kino with their singer Soi during the final years of the Soviet period, this song, released around 1989, quickly became a significant political rallying cry. It resonated deeply throughout the rapidly changing days of 1989, 1990, and 1991, embodying the widespread desire for political and social transformation. "The song is called Change, and yes, it did become something of a political rallying cry in those fast-changing days of 1989, 1990, and 1991."
